sources.title: Genome rearrangements and sorting by reversals
sources.checked_scope: Pages148–149 identify the signed Lobelia model as(−7,+1,+2,+4,+5,+3,−6,+8); the last fixed block becomes the right boundary in the seven-gene exercise. This is a mathematical model, not independent recertification of the biological mapping.
sources.bibliography_skip: Original Knox–Downie–Palmer1993 molecular mapping was not independently reread.

sources.title: Advances on sorting by reversals
sources.authors: Eric Tannier; Anne Bergeron; Marie-France Sagot
sources.checked_scope: Exact signed-reversal model on881–882, qualifications of the earlier randomized Kaplan–Verbin approach, and Theorem4 on888 plus complexity section: an actual optimal reversal sequence in O(n^(3/2)*sqrt(log n)) time.
sources.external_dependency: Full correctness of the sequence-augmentation algorithm and its specialized data structure is cited, not independently rederived in this audit.

known_changes: all3-prepre2008 replaces the p615 historical algorithm paragraph with updated primary references and the subquadratic bound.

unsigned_note.exact_result: Definition of gamma_n on149 and Theorem3 on151: unsigned reversal distance of gamma_n and its inverse is n−1.
unsigned_note.composition_convention: TAOCP Volume1 section1.3.3,p165/file180 explicitly uses left-to-right composition. The displayed product in Volume3 equals gamma_n inverse under that convention.
unsigned_note.independently_proved: Exact product mapping, the n−1 unsigned upper bound and invariance under permutation inversion.
unsigned_note.external_dependency: The Gollan lower bound is an explicitly stated primary theorem; its full proof is not independently rederived.
